section: Imperial Cholas - Vijayalaya, Rajaraja I, Rajendra I; Gangaikonda title and the naval expeditions
subsections: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Title)
a. Madurai-konda
b. Mummudi Chola
c. Ulakalanda Perumal
 d. Gangaikonda Chola

List-II (Ruler or basis)
i. Rajendra I — Ganga expedition
 ii. Parantaka I — capture of Madurai
 iii. Rajaraja I — land survey and revenue reorganisation
 iv. Rajaraja I — northern Sri Lanka named Mummadichola Mandalam

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: Madurai-konda was associated with Parantaka I's capture of Madurai; Mummudi Chola and Ulakalanda Perumal were titles of Rajaraja I; and Gangaikonda Chola was assumed by Rajendra I after the Ganga expedition.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure title–ruler pairs and then verify the reasons attached to them.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gangaikonda Chola — Rajendra I's Ganga expedition
Mummudi Chola — Rajendra I's conquest of Kadaram
Pandita Chola — Rajendra I's patronage of learning
Kadaram Kondan — Rajendra I's conquest of Kadaram
accepted.x: Mummudi Chola was a title of Rajaraja I, associated with northern Sri Lanka being named Mummadichola Mandalam. Kadaram Kondan, Pandita Chola and Gangaikonda Chola were associated with Rajendra I.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–title trap by checking whether the deed or title has been shifted to a neighbouring ruler.

accepted.s: The title ‘Kadaram Kondan’ was assumed by Rajendra I to commemorate his
accepted.x: Kadaram Kondan means the ruler associated with the conquest of Kadaram, identified with Kedah, by Rajendra I.
accepted.tq: Match the descriptive title directly with the conquest it commemorates.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rajaraja I captured Quilon after defeating the Chera navy at Trivandrum.
2. Rajaraja I annexed Madurai and broke the Pandya–Kerala–Sri Lanka confederacy.
3. Rajaraja I conquered the Maldives islands.
4. Rajaraja I placed Saktivarman and Vimaladitya as Eastern Chalukya princes in Vengi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe conquests or political actions attributed to Rajaraja I: the capture of Quilon, the subjugation of the Pandya region, the Maldives conquest and the arrangement in Vengi.
accepted.tq: When all statements concern one ruler, verify each deed separately before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Conquest or achievement)
a. Whole Sri Lanka and seizure of royal insignia
b. Complete subjugation of the Pandyas and Cheras
c. Ganga expedition of 1022 CE
 d. Kalinga, celebrated in Kalingattuparani

List-II (Ruler)
i. Kulottunga I
 ii. Rajendra I
 iii. Rajendra I
 iv. Rajendra I

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: The correct matching is a–ii, b–iv, c–iii and d–i. Rajendra I is linked with the whole-island conquest, the subjugation of the Pandyas and Cheras, and the 1022 Ganga expedition, while Kulottunga I is linked with Kalinga as celebrated in Kalingattuparani.
accepted.tq: Identify the repeated ruler among the three Rajendra I achievements, then place the distinct Kulottunga I pair.

accepted.s: Rajendra I's Ganga expedition of 1022 CE followed the route associated with
o: Kulottunga I, and defeated the ruler of Kadaram
Samudragupta, and defeated Pala Mahipala I
Parantaka I, and defeated Mahinda V
Rajaraja I, and defeated Vijayabahu I
accepted.x: Rajendra I's 1022 CE Ganga expedition followed the route associated with Samudragupta and defeated the Pala ruler Mahipala I.
accepted.tq: Separate the expedition route from other Chola conquests and apply the ruler–opponent trap.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Rajendra I's Ganga expedition
B. Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka
C. Kulottunga I sent a 72-member merchant mission to China
D. Rajendra III, the last ruler, was gone
accepted.x: Rajendra I's Ganga expedition took place in 1022 CE; Kulottunga I's China mission occurred later, Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas around 1070, and Rajendra III was gone by 1279.
accepted.tq: Fix the dated event of 1022 first, then place the later 1070 and 1279 milestones.
accepted.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

accepted.s: The Chola hold over Sri Lanka developed in which of the following ways?
o: Kulottunga I first conquered the north, and Rajendra III retained the whole island
Vijayabahu I established Chola rule over the whole island for about five decades
Rajaraja I controlled the whole island, while Rajendra I restricted Chola control to the north
Rajaraja I controlled the north, while Rajendra I extended control to the whole island for about five decades
accepted.x: Rajaraja I established Chola control in northern Sri Lanka, and Rajendra I extended it to the whole island, which remained under Chola control for about five decades.
accepted.tq: Split the comparison into ruler, territorial extent and duration instead of relying on a single familiar name.
accepted.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

accepted.s: Who expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070?
accepted.x: Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–event association rather than confusing the Sri Lankan ruler with a Chola ruler.
accepted.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Kulottunga I's foreign commercial policy?
o: He transferred the Chola capital to Kadaram to promote commerce.
He ended overseas trade and concentrated exclusively on inland revenue.
He sent a 27-member military mission to Sri Lanka.
He favoured trade and sent a 72-member merchant mission to China.
accepted.x: Kulottunga I favoured trade and sent a merchant mission consisting of 72 members to China.
accepted.tq: Pair the policy with its exact number and reject options that replace a commercial mission with a military or administrative act.
accepted.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

accepted.s: Which of the following factors contributed to the decline of the Chalukya-Cholas after Kulottunga I?
o: Complete withdrawal of the Cholas from Vengi before Kulottunga I
Strengthening of the central bureaucracy and disappearance of local chiefs
Abolition of local authority by the Pandyas
Weakening of the central bureaucracy and growth of local chieftains
accepted.x: After Kulottunga I, the central bureaucracy weakened and local chieftains grew in power. The Chalukya-Cholas subsequently declined with the rise of the Pandyas.
accepted.tq: Identify the cause–effect chain and reject the option that reverses the administrative trend.
accepted.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

accepted.s: The last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line, who was gone by 1279, was
accepted.x: Rajendra III was the last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line and was gone by 1279.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the final ruler from earlier major rulers and use the terminal date as a check.
accepted.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

accepted.s:
With reference to the Chola period, consider the following statements:
1. The Cholas were the first Indian power associated with overseas naval campaigns.
2. Chola activity helped spread Dravidian art to Southeast Asia.
3. Chola naval activity was confined to the inland waterways of Tamil country.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Cholas are described as the first Indian power with overseas naval campaigns, and their activities spread Dravidian art to Southeast Asia. Their naval activity was not confined to inland waterways.
accepted.tq: The absolute geographical restriction in statement 3 is the false comparison trap.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Chola-era Anaimangalam copper plates is correct?
o: They were returned by China during Kulottunga I's merchant mission.
They were issued by Rajendra III after the decline of the Chalukya-Cholas.
They were returned by the Netherlands at The Hague during the Prime Minister's visit in May 2026.
They were discovered during the third phase of underwater exploration off Poompuhar in September 2026.
accepted.x: The Netherlands returned the Chola-era Anaimangalam, or Leiden, copper plates at The Hague during the Prime Minister's visit in May 2026. They were ordered by Rajaraja I, engraved under Rajendra I and extended by Kulottunga I.
accepted.tq: Separate the modern repatriation event from the historical rulers connected with the inscription.

accepted.s: The Anaimangalam copper plates are associated, in sequence, with which combination of Chola rulers?
o: Ordered by Rajaraja I, engraved under Rajendra I and extended by Kulottunga I
Ordered by Rajendra I, engraved under Kulottunga I and extended by Rajendra III
Ordered by Kulottunga I, engraved under Rajaraja I and extended by Rajendra I
Ordered by Parantaka I, engraved under Rajendra I and extended by Vijayaditya VII
accepted.x: The plates originated through an order of Rajaraja I, were engraved under Rajendra I and were extended by Kulottunga I.
accepted.tq: Follow the sequence of administrative action, engraving and later extension across the three rulers.

accepted.s: The third phase of underwater exploration mentioned in connection with the early Chola capital is being conducted off
accepted.x: Tamil Nadu began the third phase of underwater exploration off Poompuhar, identified as an early Chola capital.
accepted.tq: Use the location clue and distinguish the Tamil coastal site from the Andhra Chola-period sites.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the proposed Rajaraja Chola statue and museum project?
o: A 125-metre statue at Poompuhar, planned on 52 acres at a cost of Rs 56.41 crore
A 125-foot statue at the Grand Chola Museum, Thanjavur, planned on 52 acres at a cost of Rs 56.41 crore
A 52-foot statue at the Grand Chola Museum, Thanjavur, planned on 125 acres at a cost of Rs 56.41 crore
A 125-foot statue at Rajahmundry, planned on 56.41 acres at a cost of Rs 52 crore
accepted.x: The proposed project is a 125-foot Rajaraja Chola statue at the Grand Chola Museum in Thanjavur, spread over 52 acres and costing Rs 56.41 crore.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical component—height, area and cost—before accepting the combined option.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chola–Chalukya relationship in the Andhra region:
1. Vengi was a prize in the Chola–Chalukya wars.
2. Kulottunga I united the Tamil and Andhra kingdoms.
3. The Mandalika Yugam followed from 1076 to about 1210.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Vengi was central to Chola–Chalukya rivalry; Kulottunga I united the Tamil and Andhra kingdoms; and the Mandalika Yugam followed from 1076 to approximately 1210.
accepted.tq: Treat the regional political development and its time span as separate checks before selecting the combination.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Last Eastern Chalukya — Vijayaditya VII, who died in 1279
Last Eastern Chalukya — Rajaraja I, who died in 1075
accepted.x: Kulottunga I was the first Chalukya-Chola king. Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya and died in 1075, not 1279.
accepted.tq: Check both the dynastic position and the associated date to detect the swapped ruler–date pair.

accepted.s: The last Eastern Chalukya ruler and his year of death were respectively
accepted.x: Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya ruler and died in 1075.
accepted.tq: Use the dynasty boundary clue and distinguish the 1075 date from the later Chalukya-Chola terminal date.
